constraints: The handbook fits in the selected model's context.
The desired output is a grounded answer, not an external action.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A simple pattern may not handle open-ended troubleshooting, but it is easier to evaluate and operate for this bounded use case.
details.errorCorrection: Start with the augmented LLM building block when retrieval, tools, or memory are enough and no dynamic process is required.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The handbook is an external knowledge augmentation; the answer cites the selected passage and can abstain when the source does not support it.
details.scenarioApplication: The manufacturer can update the handbook index without creating an agent loop for a question-answering task.
details.transfer: Use this pattern for manuals, FAQs, and stable internal knowledge where the response is the product and the source boundary is clear.

messages.text: The retrieval tool is useful, but exploratory agentic planning adds autonomy and a loop when the handbook already supports a bounded grounded response.
Classification and a second stage can be valid at larger scale, but the extra routing path adds latency without a stated category or ambiguity problem.
Separate research and writing agents duplicate the same source context and coordination work for a single evidence-grounded answer.

feedback.reason: Retrieval or supplied context augments a single LLM response and directly serves the grounded question. More autonomy would add complexity without a decision or action to coordinate.

options.text: An augmented LLM that receives or retrieves the handbook context and answers with a citation.
An agent with a read-only handbook retrieval tool that may explore follow-up questions before citing an answer.
A routing workflow that first classifies the question, then retrieves handbook context and renders a cited answer.
Two coordinated agents, one researching the handbook and one writing the answer, both reading the same source before responding.

prompt: A small manufacturer has a 60-page, authoritative maintenance handbook. Technicians ask questions that can be answered from the handbook, and the application should cite the relevant passage. There is no need to take actions or plan multiple steps. Which pattern is the best fit?

constraints: The number and order of searches cannot be known before the investigation.
New evidence changes the next action.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Adaptive exploration can discover relevant evidence but has less predictable cost and latency, so explicit limits and review are part of the design.
details.errorCorrection: Diagnose whether uncertainty is about the next step itself; if it is, replace a rigid sequence with an evaluated, bounded loop rather than simply adding more fixed calls.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The agent observes intermediate findings, selects a next tool call, and writes checkpoints; limits on steps, time, and spend prevent an unbounded loop.
details.scenarioApplication: The research agent should record queries and sources, pursue newly relevant leads, and stop when coverage or budget criteria are met for lead review.
details.transfer: Use agentic control for open-ended investigation, planning, or discovery only when its adaptive benefit can be measured against a bounded stop condition.

messages.text: A fixed three-call limit cannot adapt when evidence requires a different number or order of searches.
Manual follow-up leaves the system unable to execute the evidence-dependent work and does not diagnose the pattern mismatch.
Searching every possibility wastes budget and still cannot decide which follow-up matters after a discovery.

feedback.reason: The next action is evidence-dependent, so a fixed chain cannot represent the work. A bounded agent can adapt while budgets, source records, and a stopping rule keep exploration operationally safe.

options.text: Encode a fixed sequence of three search calls and truncate any investigation that needs a fourth.
Use a static retrieval prompt and let the analyst manually perform every follow-up search outside the system.
Run all possible searches in parallel before seeing evidence, then concatenate the results for Claude.
Use a bounded agentic loop that chooses the next search from evidence, records sources, and stops on explicit budget or sufficiency criteria.

prompt: A market-research assistant faces an unpredictable number of searches and follow-up paths; each discovery can change the next question. Which pattern addresses the actual failure of a fixed workflow?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Routing would omit two documents that the analyst asked to compare.
details.errorCorrection: Open-ended repetition adds no specified value or stopping criterion.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Parallelization can section independent subtasks and aggregate their results.
details.scenarioApplication: Serial dependence is not required by the stated document independence.
details.transfer: Use parallel work when subtasks are separable and the final aggregation rule is known.

messages.text: A serial dependency between summaries adds latency even though each document can be analyzed independently.
Repeated autonomous searching is unnecessary because the documents are supplied and the task is bounded.
Routing to one document omits the other two findings required by the comparison.

feedback.reason: The document-level work is independent and can be aggregated, so parallel sectioning fits the task. The shared rubric provides a consistent basis for synthesis.

options.text: A serial prompt chain that makes each document summary depend on the prior summary.
Analyze documents independently, then aggregate against the shared rubric.
An autonomous agent that repeatedly rereads all documents until it is satisfied.
A router that sends the entire request to whichever document appears most important.

prompt: A policy analyst asks Claude to compare three long documents. Each document can be reviewed independently, and the final answer must combine the three findings under a common rubric. Which pattern best matches the task?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A one-shot path discards the evidence that iteration improves the output.
details.errorCorrection: The task does not require unpredictable delegation.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluator-optimizer is useful when criteria are clear and iteration improves measurable quality.
details.scenarioApplication: Length is not a quality rubric.
details.transfer: Choose iterative refinement when its feedback signal is reliable and its marginal gain justifies another pass.

messages.text: A vote among independent drafts does not use the rubric feedback that the trials showed improves the selected draft.
The task has one known drafting objective and rubric; unpredictable delegation by paragraph adds no demonstrated value.
A one-shot call skips the feedback step that trial evidence shows improves rubric scores.

feedback.reason: The case has clear evaluation criteria and demonstrated benefit from feedback, which supports evaluator-optimizer. The revision limit keeps the loop within the observed useful range.

options.text: An evaluator-optimizer loop with the rubric and a fixed revision limit.
Generate several independent drafts and have an editor vote for one without feeding rubric feedback into a revision.
An orchestrator-worker system that invents subtasks for each paragraph.
A one-shot augmented LLM because iterative patterns are never appropriate for writing.

prompt: A content team generates a draft and can reliably score it against a detailed rubric. Trial data shows that rubric feedback usually improves the draft, while one or two revisions are enough. Which pattern should be tested?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The case requires approval before a freeze and does not authorize blanket action.
details.errorCorrection: The original alert cannot provide evidence discovered in later steps.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Agents fit open-ended work where the next steps depend on environmental feedback.
details.scenarioApplication: A fixed number of links will truncate some cases and waste work in others.
details.transfer: Separate adaptive investigation from consequential actions with their own explicit authority gate.

messages.text: A fixed two-link limit can miss relevant accounts when the path is longer and inspect unnecessary ones when it is shorter.
The initial alert cannot incorporate evidence found later in the linked-account investigation.
A temporary hold is still a consequential account action; the case requires separate approval before any freeze.

feedback.reason: The investigative path depends on findings, so a bounded agent can choose the next read step. The irreversible freeze remains behind the separate approval boundary.

options.text: A fixed workflow that inspects exactly two linked accounts in all cases.
An augmented one-shot answer using the original alert only.
Place a temporary hold on every linked account from the initial alert, then review the evidence graph before deciding which holds to keep.
A bounded agent loop for evidence-dependent read steps, with freeze approval kept as a separate action gate.

prompt: A fraud investigator’s task requires following evidence across linked accounts. The number of links varies by case, each finding determines which account to inspect next, and any account freeze needs a separate approval. Which pattern fits the investigative portion?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If one source changes the next search target, an adaptive agent may be more appropriate than fixed parallel passes.
details.errorCorrection: Each source can be evaluated separately before the evidence is combined.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Parallel sectioning handles independent perspectives; the output contract governs synthesis.
details.scenarioApplication: The final claim needs traceable source support, not agreement alone.
details.transfer: Choose parallelization when independent work adds coverage and use a defined aggregation criterion to prevent unsupported consensus.

messages.text: Routing to one source omits the independent evidence that the task requires.
Searching until agreement uses a stopping condition that favors the initial hypothesis rather than evidence sufficiency.
Serially passing prose creates dependence that the source set does not require and can propagate an early framing error.

feedback.reason: Independent analyses produce complementary findings, while the evidence aggregation rule decides what can be stated. Repeatedly searching until agreement would bias the process toward confirmation.

options.text: Route each request to one source based on the opening sentence.
Analyze sources independently; reconcile supported claims and conflicts.
Run a bounded agent that keeps searching until it agrees with its first hypothesis.
Chain each source summary into the next call so later sources inherit earlier wording.

prompt: A research assistant analyzes each source independently. Repeated trials show that separate passes catch different relevant facts, and the final answer must include a claim only when it has support in the sources. Which pattern should the team evaluate?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Completeness is already defined by deterministic checks, not subjective judgment.
details.errorCorrection: The checks have ordering and dependency requirements; concurrent execution may invalidate them.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Known steps and transitions fit a workflow with clear evaluation points.
details.scenarioApplication: Potential adaptability is not enough to justify open-ended control when the sequence is fixed.
details.transfer: Introduce agent autonomy where the next action genuinely depends on uncertain evidence or a changing task graph.

messages.text: No variable next action is described; autonomy would add a decision surface without solving an observed problem.
The checks form a sequence, so a later check may depend on an earlier validated result.
A model judgment would weaken a condition that already has a deterministic pass/fail rule.

feedback.reason: The nightly process has a known sequence and deterministic gates, so a fixed workflow is easier to validate. Adaptive selection has no demonstrated need and parallelizing dependent validations could bypass prerequisites.

options.text: Use the known workflow and outputs; add adaptation only if cases require it.
Let an agent choose each next step because it can adapt to anomalies before they occur.
Run all steps in parallel and merge the outputs at the end.
Use a general-purpose model to decide whether each payroll file is complete.

prompt: A payroll team processes the same fixed sequence every night: validate file, check totals, match employees, and produce a report. The sequence and transition rules are known, and each step has a deterministic pass/fail condition. A proposal adds an agent that chooses the next step. Which design is best supported?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A deterministic citation check remains an independent acceptance criterion and cannot be replaced by evaluator confidence.
details.errorCorrection: The case gives evidence that iterative style improvement harms source support; more iterations may worsen the required outcome.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluator-optimizer loops are useful when evaluative feedback improves drafts against the task criteria.
details.scenarioApplication: The held-out result regresses a required citation criterion, so a single bounded workflow with the existing citation gate is better supported.
details.transfer: Keep or stop iterative refinement according to measured outcomes across all required rubric dimensions, not one attractive score.

messages.text: The held-out evidence shows the revision loop regresses a required measure, so retain the successful bounded path.
Voting on prose does not validate the source citations or resolve the measured regression.
Evaluator confidence is not a substitute for the required deterministic citation check.

feedback.reason: An evaluator-optimizer is justified only when feedback improves the task’s required criteria. Here the loop optimizes style while violating a citation floor, so the fixed bounded path and citation check are better supported.

options.text: Continue revising until the evaluator gives its highest style score, regardless of citation changes.
Add parallel workers to vote on which draft sounds more authoritative.
Replace the citation check with evaluator confidence because it is cheaper to compute.
Keep a bounded draft workflow with the citation gate; stop the evaluator-optimizer loop because its measured revision regresses a required outcome.

prompt: A writing assistant generates a report draft and then asks an evaluator to score style and completeness. On held-out cases, one revision improves style but reduces citation support below the release floor; the original draft plus a deterministic citation check passes. What pattern should the architect retain for this task?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An agent may be justified if evidence changes the tools or sequence required; that fact is absent here.
details.errorCorrection: Calling every conditional flow an agent overlooks the distinction between a known branch and open-ended next-action selection.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Workflow orchestration is suited to predefined steps and transitions; agentic control is useful when actions must be selected dynamically.
details.scenarioApplication: The API result selects one of two specified paths, and validation and writes remain explicit.
details.transfer: Ask whether the path is specified before execution or must be discovered from evolving results.

messages.text: A branch in a known state machine does not make the next action open-ended; autonomous choice adds unnecessary variation.
The task has a stable sequence and data contract, so worker negotiation does not solve an unresolved decomposition problem.
A prompt cannot replace the required identity, policy, validation, and write boundaries.

feedback.reason: The sequence and exception handoff are known in advance. A fixed workflow can express the branch without granting an agent authority to choose arbitrary actions.

options.text: Use a fixed workflow with explicit branches and deterministic checks.
An autonomous agent that chooses the next action and tool at every stage.
A multi-agent swarm in which each worker decides which fields to extract.
A single prompt asking Claude to perform the full process and confirm the write.

prompt: A loan-intake process always validates identity, extracts six fields, checks a policy API, then writes a case record. If the API says ‘manual review,’ the same known handoff runs; no step chooses new tools or invents follow-up tasks. Which pattern best fits?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The agentic branch still needs stopping conditions, evidence requirements, and a human or deterministic execution boundary if policy changes are consequential.
details.errorCorrection: Choosing one architecture for all requests ignores the different decision structures of the 96% and 4% slices.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A hybrid pattern uses a workflow for stable paths and delegates only the variable path to an agent with explicit tool and action limits.
details.scenarioApplication: Exact matches use the template; absent or conflicting records enter the two-source investigation and return a recommendation.
details.transfer: Segment the workload by actual uncertainty and apply the least variable control that can resolve each slice.

messages.text: The exact lookup does not resolve the 4% conflicts or missing-record cases; always returning could misstate policy.
It pays the agentic cost on the routine path even though the next step is already known.
Parallel work does not help cases that need no investigation and can duplicate a simple exact lookup.

feedback.reason: The evidence separates a large known path from a smaller path whose next source depends on findings. Route by the observed state and keep the investigation bounded and non-executing.

options.text: Use a single fixed chain for all requests and always answer from the first retrieved record.
Use an open-ended agent for every request, including the 96% exact-match path.
Use parallel workers on all cases, even when the exact record already resolves the question.
Keep the exact-match workflow; bound investigation to unresolved or conflicting cases.

prompt: A service retrieves the exact policy record for 96% of requests and answers those from a fixed template. For the remaining 4%, an absent or contradictory record triggers a live investigation across two sources; the search path depends on what the first source returns. The investigation may recommend, but cannot execute, a change. Which architecture fits this evidence?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the exception search becomes the normal case and its next action depends on findings, reassess whether the flexible branch should expand.
details.errorCorrection: A free-form loop across all cases adds choices to a sequence whose order and checks are already known.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Use fixed workflows for stable sequences and bounded agentic behavior when a step depends on discoveries.
details.scenarioApplication: The workflow can retain mandatory status and eligibility checks while routing missing policy evidence into a bounded search path.
details.transfer: Separate stable process control from evidence-dependent investigation.

messages.text: The required sequence and deterministic eligibility rule do not need model-selected steps on every request.
A changing bulletin can be retrieved when needed; loading all versions risks stale or irrelevant context.
Missing evidence is not proof of ineligibility; the exception requires retrieval or an explicit unresolved state.

feedback.reason: The main path is known and has a deterministic eligibility gate; only the evidence-gathering exception needs bounded flexibility. That preserves control while allowing investigation where facts are missing.

options.text: Keep the fixed steps in a workflow; use bounded search only when policy evidence is missing.
Make every return an autonomous agent loop so the model can choose whether to check status and eligibility.
Load a versioned bulletin index with the prompt and rely on the model to choose the relevant revision.
Use a fixed workflow for every case and return “ineligible” when the policy clause is absent.

prompt: A returns workflow has a fixed sequence: retrieve the policy, check order status, apply a deterministic eligibility rule, then produce a structured recommendation. A small number of cases require searching a changing product bulletin when a policy clause is missing. Which architecture fits the evidence?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If policy explicitly permits an alternative authoritative source, encode and validate that source as a supported exception.
details.errorCorrection: Confidence is not a substitute for required source evidence or a mandatory validation contract.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Architecture may vary the evidence-gathering path while preserving required deterministic gates and outcome states.
details.scenarioApplication: The unreadable attachment should produce an explicit exception, not an inferred value or skipped approval check.
details.transfer: Keep exception routing explicit and preserve the same approval requirements across architecture patterns.

messages.text: Confidence does not authorize skipping a mandatory field or validation.
Vendor history may not establish the current supplier fact; inference hides the missing evidence.
A second model agent does not make an unreadable source legible or define which validations can be skipped.

feedback.reason: An unreadable source creates an evidence gap, not permission to bypass a mandatory validation. The fixed process can still route that case to a bounded exception path.

options.text: Allow confidence-based skips only for low-risk fields, with a sample review to estimate the miss rate.
Keep the workflow fixed and silently infer missing attachment fields from vendor history.
Keep required steps fixed; route unreadable attachments to review and require every validation before approval.
Make the entire intake a multi-agent process so a second agent can validate the first agent’s conclusion.

prompt: A procurement intake has a fixed schema and four mandatory steps. In 8% of cases a supplier attachment is unreadable; the team proposes an agent that may skip validation if it believes the other fields are sufficient. Which design preserves the useful flexibility without changing the decision contract?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If evidence search becomes common and has variable follow-ups, broaden only that branch and keep the required checks enforced.
details.errorCorrection: A frequently observed sequence does not make mandatory controls safe to omit or reorder.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A workflow fits known ordered steps; agentic decisions are useful where the next action depends on new evidence.
details.scenarioApplication: The extra search is conditional, while the core identity and eligibility stages are fixed.
details.transfer: Express invariants as explicit gates and place flexibility at the uncertain branch.

messages.text: A log of skipped mandatory stages does not make those controls optional or guarantee the decision contract.
A prompt rule is not equivalent to a separately enforced eligibility check.
Parallel agents do not remove the stated dependency order and add coordination without changing the evidence need.

feedback.reason: The stable mandatory sequence should remain explicit. The rare evidence-dependent branch can be flexible without making required identity, policy, and eligibility steps optional.

options.text: Keep the four mandatory stages in a workflow and add a bounded evidence-search branch for the missing-clause exception.
Let the agent choose the next stage when earlier results make the usual sequence unnecessary, while logging skipped steps.
Replace the eligibility check with a prompt rule so the loop can complete the route in one turn.
Run each stage as an independent agent, then have a lead reconcile identity, policy, and eligibility results.

prompt: A claims route follows: identity lookup → policy retrieval → deterministic eligibility check → structured recommendation. A proposed agent loop can choose which step to run. The workflow has had no valid reason to skip or reorder a step in 2,000 cases; exceptions require one extra evidence search. What is the best architecture?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the evidence source set and query sequence later become stable, a fixed retrieval workflow may be simpler.
details.errorCorrection: Variable evidence does not justify making unrelated mandatory steps optional or removing controls.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Use a hybrid pattern when fixed process invariants surround an evidence-dependent search.
details.scenarioApplication: The filings can change follow-up queries; stop conditions and budget bound that variability.
details.transfer: Reassess patterns when the dependency structure changes, not merely when input content is unstructured.

messages.text: This is a safe bounded fallback but fails to use evidence-dependent follow-up when filings lead to new queries.
The reviewer does not replace the stated stop rule and budget needed to bound the search.
Parallel work cannot bypass prerequisites when later steps depend on earlier outputs.

feedback.reason: The discovery path varies with what each filing reveals, but the required intake gates have not changed. Bounded flexibility belongs inside the evidence-gathering stage.

options.text: Keep the core workflow fixed and make the filing lookup a single deterministic query; route any unresolved search to review.
Let an agent search freely across filings until it finds enough evidence, then ask a reviewer to approve the conclusion.
Keep required gates fixed and bound the variable filing search by a stop rule and budget.
Use parallel workers for each required intake step even though later steps depend on earlier results.

prompt: An intake system has the same four required steps as the previous pilot, but now supplier evidence is discovered through a changing set of public filings. Each filing may lead to a new query, and the search stops when a defined evidence threshold is met or the budget expires. What changed enough to justify a flexible component?

constraints: The common 80% has a stable, bounded path.
The 20% needs adaptive discovery and its own budget and review boundary.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Two paths add routing and maintenance overhead, but they avoid paying agentic cost on routine work while retaining discovery where it creates value.
details.errorCorrection: Do not let a minority of open-ended cases force all traffic through an agent or let a stable path hide missing evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A classifier or explicit request type selects the augmented workflow or bounded agent; each path has its own evaluation, permissions, and stop conditions.
details.scenarioApplication: Measure FAQ accuracy and latency separately from investigation coverage, source quality, and budget, and send uncertain routing or agent completion to review.
details.transfer: Segment workloads by whether the next action is predictable and then evaluate a workflow and an agentic path against their actual slices.

messages.text: Universal agentic execution spends exploratory cost on routine questions and makes the stable workload less predictable.
The fixed knowledge base cannot supply evidence for the investigation slice and would produce confident incompleteness.
Answer length is not a quality or evidence criterion, and duplicate execution doubles cost without a route decision.

feedback.reason: The workload has two distinct decision structures: most cases have a known retrieval-and-answer path, while a minority benefits from adaptive search. Routing keeps each pattern proportionate.

options.text: Route stable questions through an augmented workflow and send investigation cases to a bounded agentic path with explicit stop and review criteria.
Use the agentic path for every question so the system has one architecture and can discover new sources when needed.
Use the fixed knowledge base for every question and return its best passage when investigation evidence is missing.
Run both paths for every request and select the longer answer as the more complete result.

prompt: A support service handles 80% of questions with a stable knowledge base and fixed answer format. The remaining 20% require investigation across changing sources and follow-up searches. Which architecture should route the two workloads?

constraints: Normal intake steps and output schema are fixed.
Only the exception branch needs adaptive evidence search; the final policy check is deterministic.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The hybrid design requires explicit branching and monitoring, but it avoids unnecessary agent cost and protects the release gate.
details.errorCorrection: Place adaptive behavior at the smallest branch that requires discovery, while retaining deterministic gates around the external decision.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The workflow produces a typed intake and a flag; the agent searches relevant evidence under limits, and ordinary code enforces the final policy contract.
details.scenarioApplication: Process routine records through fixed stages, route flagged exceptions with their context and budget, and quarantine any record failing the final check.
details.transfer: When only exceptions are open-ended, use a predictable workflow as the spine and isolate adaptive search behind a measured, bounded branch.

messages.text: Applying exploration to every intake ignores the fixed normal path and raises cost and variability without evidence.
Manual exception work loses the opportunity for a controlled adaptive branch and leaves the state unobservable.
A citation can be stale or inapplicable; it does not replace the deterministic policy check.

feedback.reason: The normal path is known and the exception path is evidence-dependent. A workflow plus a bounded subpath preserves deterministic validation while granting exploration only where needed.

options.text: Send every intake through an open-ended agent so routine records and exceptions share one adaptive path.
Use one fixed prompt and have analysts investigate exceptions manually without recording an exception state.
Implement a workflow for extraction and validation, invoke a bounded agent only on flagged exceptions, then run the policy check before release.
Skip the policy check when the exception agent returns a cited passage because citation presence proves compliance.

prompt: A compliance intake has a fixed extraction, validation, and schema sequence. Only exceptions require searching a changing evidence store, and all final records pass a deterministic policy check. Which architecture is most appropriate?

constraints: The next read tool and number of checks depend on live equipment readings.
Inspection tools are read-only, but the proposed repair is consequential.
Safety thresholds, deterministic checks, and human approval must stop the action path.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every answer came only from the handbook and no live tool or action were needed, retain the augmented LLM boundary in CCARP-D01-O03-boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Static handbook context cannot execute or adapt to live evidence, and inference from absent readings can produce an unsafe repair recommendation.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says agents fit open-ended problems whose number of steps cannot be predicted and describes them as LLMs using tools in a loop. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The action path has evidence-dependent steps and a consequential approval boundary, unlike a one-shot cited handbook answer.
details.scenarioApplication: Use a bounded agentic loop for read-only inspection with explicit stop conditions, then pass the proposed repair and evidence through deterministic checks and human approval before action.
details.transfer: Use measured evidence and the stated authority boundary to choose the least complex design that satisfies the workload's constraint; revisit the route when the counterfactual changes.

messages.text: Static handbook context cannot execute or adapt to live evidence, and inference from absent readings can produce an unsafe repair recommendation.
A single unrestricted call has no explicit stop conditions or enforceable approval boundary for the consequential repair.
This avoids the adaptive inspection the scenario requires and escalates routine evidence gathering instead of using bounded read-only checks.

feedback.reason: The required pattern changes when the system must choose follow-up tools from new evidence; the action boundary remains outside unrestricted model control.

options.text: Use a bounded read-only agent loop, then require deterministic checks and human approval before repair.
Use the augmented LLM handbook path and ask the technician to infer the live reading and next action from the answer.
Expose all read and repair tools in one call and let the model choose the repair action whenever readings suggest it.
Use a fixed checklist and escalate every case to a technician without inspecting live readings through tools.

prompt:
Technicians ask a maintenance question from a handbook and may then inspect live equipment, select among read tools based on readings, stop at a safety threshold, and request approval before a repair action.

Which interaction pattern fits the evidence-dependent inspection and repair boundary?

constraints: An exact lookup resolves 94% of requests at 220 ms p95 under a 500 ms synchronous SLA.
Only no-match or conflicting records create the evidence gap; research is five times more expensive.
Research has a separate three-minute asynchronous contract with pending and human escalation states.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the exact lookup never produced a no-match or conflict, remove the asynchronous research job; if the business accepted one three-minute response for every request, re-evaluate the synchronous routing boundary.
details.errorCorrection: The evidence gap is known only after the exact lookup, and inline research would violate the routine 500 ms contract when the catalog can resolve the request.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Just-in-time retrieval uses lightweight identifiers to load detailed information only when relevant, keeping context focused. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: Keep the 500 ms synchronous contract for routine exact lookups and defer the expensive research branch to an explicit asynchronous path only after the lookup proves an evidence gap.
details.scenarioApplication: Run the exact structured lookup synchronously, return its grounded result when it succeeds, and enqueue a bounded agentic research job only on a no-match or conflict state; expose pending, completion, citations, cost, and the three-minute timeout rather than running research inline.
details.transfer: Use an authoritative exact-key lookup first when it resolves the common path within the SLA; route no-match or conflicting evidence to a separately bounded research path.

messages.text: The evidence gap is known only after the exact lookup, and inline research would violate the routine 500 ms contract when the catalog can resolve the request.
Always researching wastes the cheap deterministic path and turns 94% of requests into unnecessary asynchronous work.
A no-match is the trigger for bounded research or human handling; a provisional semantic result does not satisfy the grounded-answer and evidence-state contract.

feedback.reason: The routing decision is between a fast synchronous first stage and a deferred evidence-gap job with its own SLA, not a generic choice to make every hard request agentic.

options.text: Classify the user message as routine or investigative before lookup and run the research loop inline for messages that appear complex.
Perform the exact lookup synchronously; research asynchronously only after a no-match or conflict, with explicit pending and timeout states.
Always enqueue the three-minute research job, even when the exact lookup succeeds, so every response has the same evidence depth.
Return the top semantic result immediately when the exact lookup has no match and mark its citation as provisional.

prompt:
A product-support workflow first performs an exact SKU and warranty-status lookup. For 94% of requests it returns a grounded answer in 220 ms p95 under a 500 ms synchronous SLA; for 6% it returns no active match or conflicting records. A research pilot improves accepted resolution on that evidence-gap slice from 61% to 79% but costs five times as much.

Which routing design preserves the synchronous contract while using research where it adds value?

constraints: The subtasks and their order are known in advance.
A deterministic style gate must run before publication.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Explicit stages require orchestration code and intermediate storage, but they provide reproducible gates and clearer failure localization.
details.errorCorrection: Choose a workflow when the path is predictable; reserve agentic loops for cases where the next action genuinely depends on discovery.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Each Claude call performs one bounded transformation, and the application controls the sequence and style validator between calls.
details.scenarioApplication: Research output feeds the draft call, the draft feeds the style check, and a failed check returns a structured revision request rather than publication.
details.transfer: Map known business steps and mandatory gates before selecting an architecture; the pattern should follow process uncertainty, not novelty.

messages.text: Autonomous planning adds variability and cost without addressing a missing step in this fixed process.
One response hides stage failures and gives no independent style gate before publication.
Routing chooses among paths but does not represent the required order or enforce the fixed validation gate.

feedback.reason: Known subtasks and ordering favor a workflow whose stages and gate are explicit. Prompt chaining makes each handoff testable and avoids paying for unneeded autonomous planning.

options.text: Use an open-ended agent that chooses its own research and revision loop even though every required step and gate is already known.
Use a prompt-chained workflow with explicit research, drafting, and style-validation steps, passing structured output between them.
Use a single unrestricted prompt that asks Claude to research, draft, and self-approve the article in one response.
Use a routing layer that sends each article to whichever specialist appears most relevant, without encoding the fixed sequence.

prompt: An editorial service must draft an article from a fixed outline, run a known sequence of research and drafting steps, and pass a fixed style gate before publication. Which architecture is the best fit?

constraints: Most messages map to stable categories and category-specific paths.
Ambiguous classification needs a human route rather than an invented action.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Routing is less flexible for novel requests and requires category maintenance, but it gives predictable permissions and a controlled human path.
details.errorCorrection: Use routing when known categories have distinct procedures; design uncertainty as a first-class branch rather than force a best guess.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A classifier selects a bounded category path; the route can carry uncertainty to a human or refuse execution rather than turn a low-confidence label into a side effect.
details.scenarioApplication: Delivery, damaged-item, and access messages each invoke their approved policy/API path, while unresolved classification enters a review queue with the evidence shown.
details.transfer: For operations with stable classes and materially different actions, separate classification, routing, and ambiguity handling before considering a free-form agent.

messages.text: Exploring all tools on every message spends cost and exposes unnecessary actions when the normal paths are already known.

A shared path does not enforce the distinct category policy and API contract before a side effect; deferring ambiguity to a post-action exception can send a sensitive or invalid request to the wrong route.
A description without a route leaves the operational work undone and does not enforce the category-specific policy.
Without category routing, the known policy/API paths cannot be selected consistently or evaluated as bounded workflows.
Without a pre-action ambiguity route, uncertain requests are forced into a category-specific operation instead of reaching a human safely.

feedback.reason: Stable categories justify a routing step, while ambiguity needs an explicit safe state at the route boundary. Together they prevent exploratory tool use and false certainty.

options.text: Let one agent explore every support tool for every message so it can discover the best category at runtime.
Classify the request, route it to the corresponding policy and API workflow, and use a confidence or ambiguity state for human handoff.
Apply one general support workflow and shared policy/API surface to every category, then send exceptions to a human after the workflow has attempted the request.
Use one fixed prompt for all categories and ask Claude to describe the next API call without executing a route.
Route ambiguous or low-confidence messages to a human queue with the evidence and candidate categories, without invoking a category-specific API.

prompt: A support platform has stable delivery, damaged-item, and account-access categories, each with its own API and policy path. Ambiguous messages must reach a human. Which TWO design choices fit this workload? Select TWO.
